title: Natural Selection
seo_title: Grade 8 Natural Selection Worksheets: Variation, Survival, Adaptation and Population Data
standard_text: Construct an explanation based on evidence that describes how genetic variations of traits in a population increase some individuals' probability of surviving and reproducing in a specific environment.
meta_desc: Free middle school science worksheets on natural selection (NGSS MS-LS4-4, MS-LS4-6): variation, competition, survival and reproduction, and using percentages and graphs to show how traits change in populations. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Helpful inherited traits become more common.
key_sub: Individuals with traits that fit their environment survive and reproduce more, so those traits increase over generations.
body_html:
How to think about it

Natural selection works like this:

  1. Variation: individuals have different inherited traits.
  2. Overproduction and competition: more offspring are born than can survive.
  3. Selection: individuals with traits that help in that environment survive and reproduce more.
  4. Inheritance: they pass the helpful traits on, so the percent of the population with the trait increases over generations.

Individuals do not change their traits because they need to. A trait that helps in one place may hurt in another.

Example

Dark moths go from 10% to 70% on sooty trees. Change?

70 − 10

Answer: 60 percentage points

Example

Why did dark moths increase?

Camouflage from birds.

Answer: They survived and reproduced more.

Common mistakes

  • Thinking individuals change their traits because they need to.
  • Thinking the strongest always survive. Fitness means surviving and reproducing.
  • Thinking a helpful trait helps in every environment.

faq.a: Individuals vary in inherited traits. Those with traits that help in their environment survive and reproduce more, so the traits become more common over generations.

faq.q: Do animals change their traits because they need to?
faq.a: No. Traits vary because of genes. Natural selection changes how common each trait is in a population over many generations.

faq.q: How can math show natural selection?
faq.a: By tracking the percent of a population with a trait over generations, using tables and graphs to see whether it increases or decreases.

items.q: Why are antibiotic-resistant bacteria a growing problem?
c: Antibiotics make bacteria stronger.
Resistance is learned.
Bacteria choose to become resistant.
Antibiotics kill non-resistant bacteria, so resistant ones survive and multiply.
items.e: Natural selection in action.

items.q: Owen studies a population of lizards with longer legs or shorter legs on an island with wide tree trunks and open ground. Which individuals are most likely to survive and reproduce?
c: those with longer legs
only the oldest ones
those with shorter legs
all of them equally
items.e: The trait that helps in this environment is longer legs.

items.q: Why do most species produce more offspring than can survive?
c: They want large families.
Limited food and space create competition, so only some survive.
Every offspring survives.
It makes the environment bigger.
items.e: Overproduction leads to competition.

items.q: Kai studies giraffes where lower leaves are eaten and higher leaves remain. Why do individuals with longer necks leave more offspring?
c: They are always the strongest.
Their trait appeared because they needed it.
They decided to change their trait.
Their trait helps them survive long enough to reproduce and pass it on.
items.e: Natural selection acts on traits that already vary.
